relationships.subject: Cav3.2
relationships.evidence_quote: eliminating the putative physiological target eliminated the analgesic effects of camphene and alpha-bisabolol, thus confirming that Cav3.2 channels are required for the in vivo actions of the two terpenes

relationships.subject: camphene
relationships.evidence_quote: Injury to the sciatic nerve triggered a robust reduction in mechanical withdrawal threshold that was partially reversed upon intrathecal delivery of camphene or alpha-bisabolol

key_findings: Camphene and alpha-bisabolol partially inhibit Cav3.2 (IC50 7.7 and 4.5 uM) and shift half-inactivation hyperpolarized.
Intrathecal terpenes are analgesic in formalin, CFA and nerve injury models; CFA effect is absent in Cav3.2 null mice and sex independent.
